'''''Pleiospilos nelii''''', the '''split rock''', '''splitrock''' or '''living granite''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Stone Plant (Pleiospilos spp.) - Plants {{!}} Candide Gardening |url=https://candidegardening.com/GB/plants/2dbc266c-1b9c-4e2b-b8a5-edda4bc97ac1 |website=Candide |access-date=31 May 2021}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Aizoaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to South Africa. It grows in semi-arid areas with rainfall of between 150mm and 300mm, in the [[Karoo]] of South Africa.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/SUCCULENTS/Family/Aizoaceae/14724/Pleiospilos_nelii
| title = Pleiospilos nelii | website = Encyclopedia of Succulents | publisher = Llife | access-date = 15 February 2021}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The [[botanical name#Binary name|species epithet]] ''nelii'' honours the South African botanist [[Gert Cornelius Nel]]. The common name "split rock" refers to the appearance of the plant's leaves.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantnop/pleiospilosnelii.htm | title = Pleiospilos nelii }}</ref>

==Description==
''Pleiospilos nelii'' is a [[succulent plant|succulent]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] which can reach a height of {{convert|5|-|8|cm|0|abbr=on}} and a diameter of about {{convert|10|cm|0|abbr=on}}. This very short-stemmed, nearly stemless plant has one or more pairs of opposite, almost hemispherical, grey-green or brownish leaves. The surface of the leaves has many small dark spots. A new pair of leaves is produced each year, replacing an older pair. This plant closely resembles a small cracked rock (hence the common name), an appearance which may have evolved as a defence against [[herbivory]]. The superficially [[asteraceae|daisy]]-like flowers are yellow-orange, {{convert|6|-|7.5|cm|0|abbr=on}} across, and emerge from the plant's [[Bud#Types of buds|apical bud]]. The flowers are large in relation to the size of the plant. Each flower opens in the afternoon and closes at sunset, over a bloom period of several days.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''P. nelii'' is one of several plants cultivated for their rocklike appearance. They are sometimes collectively called [[Aizoaceae|mesembs]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://files.nyu.edu/ms689/public/AGM.html#pleiospilos |title= The New Mastering the Art of Growing Mesembs by Steven Hammer|website=files.nyu.edu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811183847/https://files.nyu.edu/ms689/public/AGM.html |archive-date=2014-08-11}}</ref> In [[temperateness|temperate]] regions it is grown under glass for protection from excessive rain and hard freezes. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Pleiospilos nelii ''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/131621/Pleiospilos-nelii/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 80 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 7 May 2018}}</ref>
